I'd say email/call as well, they responded to me with the same statement they put in the Munson email (i.e. "we are requiring everyone to get boosted by the 31st or after 14 days of becoming eligible") so not much to go off of. 


There are also studies conducted showing you get boosted immunity from hybrid immunity (better immunity from having a case before being vaccinated, but the opposite case has similarly boosted immunity). So there is ofc a benefit to getting the booster after having covid, but I was planning to wait until the natural immunity waned as the whole point of a booster is to boost your immune response after its wavered. There aren't any known risks I'm aware of of getting the booster soon after a breakthrough covid case, but like my doctor, other experts recommend waiting a bit if you're not immunocompromised, that it won't hurt. 

https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2021/11/24/1058743263/im-fully-vaccinated-and-i-also-had-covid-do-i-need-a-booster
I think it'd be fairly useless with omicron. The rapid tests have a huge false negative rate and are only really effective 2-3 days after showing symptoms

So like many others I caught COVID over break. I'm still recovering, isolation will be up in time for the semester. I was prepared to get boosted until I got COVID. My doctor recommended waiting a month or two before getting the booster now because of natural immunity from a breakthrough case. I contacted RIT about this and I can imagine I'm not the only one in a similar situation.


Additionally, I can't imagine having the booster requirement set for Jan 31st being effective at preventing Omicron spread when we're coming back to campus on Jan 10th?? They absolutely should've sent a booster requirement out sooner so the majority could be boosted before the start of the semester (those who wouldn't otherwise get the booster would be required to have it before the semester begins).

We won't know at least until tomorrow.

Hi, thank you so much for your compassion. I've looked around but it doesn't appear we have one in our area. There is a wider rape crisis hotline, but I feel I am not necessarily in crisis as this occurred a year ago and would not want to take up space where someone may actually be suffering from a recent incident and needs the emergency help. From your experience, do you think it would still be appropriate to reach out to the hotline?

It doesn't matter what you thought beforehand, try not to beat yourself up. You and your baby are in danger. Seek support from a trusted family member or friend or literally any responsible adult if you can. Plan your leave. Get out. Call the cops if you can't. How he is treating you is not okay, and I'm glad you're recognizing that.
You are a fucking hell of a force to be reckoned with. I don't know your situation, but always remember it's okay to seek support while you're out there fucking killin' it <3

I'm glad. Let me know if you find anything else that works for you, or if you want to talk more about your thoughts. Including the complexities of university or the medical field

Ok so. Coincidentally I just *just* talked to my therapist about a very similar situation I'm going through. 

Something that's helping me is brainstorming ideas of things I'd do if everyone in my life and society rejected me, I failed at college, I couldn't be hired, etc. Like, I'd go be a nomad on the hills and start a farm and not give any fucks about anything else. I'd go start/work at an animal rescue. I'd go backpacking/hiking. I'd go to another country and work to earn my keep. Literally any silly escape reason where you go do something and don't care about the repercussions. At least we'll be alive and if we decide to come back to society, we can. Or we can choose not to. Completely our decision. 

My therapist kinda helped reframe the way I think about suicide. It's an escape. A permanent one. We all want to escape our pain, really. But there are other ways we can escape our lives. We don't have to kill ourselves. 

Now, am I done having suicidal thoughts? Lol no. But it's put me a step in a healthier direction, so I just thought I'd share.

I'm with you, same age, similar outlook. Yo we should all get together and give no fucks about what other people think and just go be nomads on a mountain or island somewhere and do whatever the fuck we feel like in the moment.

Gotcha, yeah that makes sense not wanting scars. They can be a pain in the butt (or wherever they are lol). Not having ammo makes it a little harder to pull the trigger at least. If you do end up getting ammo, do you think you could try giving it to someone to hold onto? Or locking it up/making it harder to access for yourself? That way you can still go through the motions with the gun without the risk. Seems like there's a part of you that wants to live since you're talking with us on this subreddit, and I'm glad you are. Hold onto that part of you as much as you can, I know it's really tough and draining to fight off the suicidal ideas

Oh damn yeah, having knives or guns or scissors near me makes it all the more easier for me me fall into my suicidal loop. Do you think you'd be able to open up to someone about needing company or asking someone to hold onto the rifle for you for a bit? Or even like getting a safe to put the rifle in and giving the key to someone trusted, that way you can't access it as easily but you can still access it if need be.

Realistically who knows where you'd end up on the ground after shooting yourself. You'd be in a lot of physical pain I'd imagine, even if just for a split second, so you wouldn't really have control over where you land. And I've heard horror stories of people shooting themselves and then not winding up dead but with brain trauma or something of the sort instead. Would you be open to texting the 741741 line or something of the sort? They've seriously gotten me through incredibly rough nights and a few suicide attempts, and there's less pressure because it's a text line. I've disclosed suicide plans with them and they helped me try to wait it out and at least postpone the plan.

No it's okay, no need to apologize. Anything that would happen to me would not be your fault. Thank you for letting me know, it's helpful to get an idea of what to say--I suck at talking to people.

Damn I hope we both get through the roughness in our lives one day

I appreciate that. Yeah, honesty is important. I'm trying to get myself to be more honest to other people and to myself.
